verdict.rationale: Paperspace documents creating GPU machines through the console, API, or CLI, and connecting over SSH with root access. Its "ML in a Box" template comes with ML frameworks and CUDA drivers preinstalled, so code can run right after provisioning. Speed rests on a vendor claim ("signup to training a model in seconds"), high-end GPUs such as the H100 require approval, and one hands-on user called getting SSH access "an uphill battle" on Core servers. missing for 10: independent corroboration of minutes-scale provisioning-to-running time, instant on-demand access to high-end GPUs without approval, evidence that SSH setup is reliably smooth.

support.subject: As a developer, I can provision an on-demand GPU instance from the console or API and be running code on it within minutes

citations.quote: You can create a Linux machine using the Paperspace console, Paperspace API, or Paperspace CLI.
Machines are Linux and Windows virtual machines with persistent storage, GPU options, and free unlimited bandwidth.
Bring your SSH key and connect directly to your VM with full root access.
Choose "ML in a Box" template that comes preinstalled with all the major ML frameworks and CUDA® drivers.
Go from signup to training a model in seconds
